proof: For theta in S^2 define g_theta(r)=1_S(x0+r theta)+1_S(x0-r theta), 0<=r<=R, so 0<=g_theta<=2 and the full line length is integral_0^R g_theta(r) dr.

If every central line had length >2 delta R, then among all g in [0,2] with integral g>2 delta R the weighted moment integral g(r) r^2 dr is minimized by packing g=2 nearest r=0, hence is > 2 delta^3 R^3/3.
Spherical coordinates give |S|=(1/2) integral_{S^2} integral_0^R g_theta(r) r^2 dr dtheta > delta^3 |B_R|.
Contraposition with delta=epsilon^(1/3) proves the claim.
lemma.sharpness: The exponent 1/3 and constant 1 are sharp for this information: S=B(x0,epsilon^(1/3)R) has volume fraction epsilon and every central line has fraction epsilon^(1/3).
lemma.statement: If S is measurable in B(x0,R) and |S|/|B_R| <= epsilon, then there exists a unit d with |S intersect (x0-Rd,x0+Rd)|/(2R) <= epsilon^(1/3). For open S this is exactly the geometric form needed by Grujic Definition 4.1.
verification: no PDE, pressure, Lorentz/Morrey, or regularity input is used

outer_to_inner_bridge.statement: Choose the direction supplied by the cube-root lemma on the outer ball B(x0,R), but evaluate the same line on the inner consumer segment of radius r=a0 Omega_t^(-1/2). Since the inner high-set length is at most the outer high-set length, its relative fraction is at most min(1,(A/a0) epsilon_A^(1/3)).
